newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Brewer of Jamaica's Red Stripe beer itself in red.
newsitem.headline: Brewer of Jamaica's Red Stripe beer itself in red.

text.p: The Jamaican brewery Desnoes & Geddes, bottlers of Red Stripe brand beer, which has struggled for profitability over the past there years, Monday announced a loss for the first half of 1996.
The company, majority-owned by Guinness Plc, posted a J$170.9 million ($4.9 million) loss for the first half, compared with a J$155.6 million ($4 million) profit for the first half of 1995.
Most of the reversal was the result of interest charges, which the company said jumped 300 percent from last June 30 to June 30, 1996.

Red Stripe, an international favourite of fans of reggae music and other aspects of Jamaica's popular culture, controls about 50 percent of Jamaica's beer market, and is exported to 22 countries in North America, Europe, Asia and the Caribbean.

Desnoes & Geddes also is in the midst of a 10-year expansion programme that is expected to cost J$5 billion ($143 million), in which it plans to increase exports to the United States by 400 percent within two years.
The brewery has struggled for profitability over the past three years, as Jamaica's economic stagnation has cut into sales of Desnoes & Geddes beer, stout and soft drinks.
